newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Telecom signs GSM deal with U.S. partners.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Telecom signs GSM deal with U.S. partners.

text.p: Slovenske Telekomunikacie s.p. (ST), the state-owned telecom monopoly, on Friday said it had signed a GSM agreement with its two U.S. partners.
ST spokesman Lubomir Stancel said Slovak Telecom will hold 60 percent in the new company, with U.S. West Media Group Inc and Bell Atlantic Corp sharing the remaining 40 percent.
"We have just signed the agreement on the creation of Eurotel Bratislava a.s., a joint-stock company, which will operate the second Slovak GSM network," Stancel told Reuters.

The three companies already operate the country's sole mobile telephone network, the NMT analogue system, through a joint-venture Eurotel sro, in which ST holds 51 percent and the two U.S. telecom groups together hold 49 percent.
Stancel said the new company will be completely independent and that the only thing in common with Eurotel sro are its owners.

Negotiations over the second Slovak GSM operator have dragged since July, when the three partners agreed on creation of a new company, but had to reach a final framework for the venture which would conform to the government's 60 percent Slovak ownership condition.
In September, the Slovak Ministry of Telecommunications formally granted one of the two planned GSM licences to Eurotel sro, as stipulated by the contract for the NMT system signed in 1991.

The second Slovak GSM network will be operated by Slovtel GSM a.s., a consortium of four Slovak energy companies, the state monopoly gas distributor and a private firm Hanco sro, which teamed up with France Telecom.
